110	
111	The issuer checks activation identity, exact subject/basis, result variant,

933	## 11. The activation packet
934	
935	An actor receives one activated frame or one declared active frame
936	configuration, never an implied demand to reconstruct the complete
937	workspace from ambient context (P0). The minimum
938	activation packet contains:
939	
940	- frame identity and revision;
941	- the evaluation and its result algebra;
942	- the exact subject and basis;
943	- the material relations and applicable invariants;
944	- semantic, evaluation, operation where material, and decision authority;
945	- admissible evidence and tools;
946	- the capability and context envelope;
947	- exclusions and prohibited assumptions;
948	- declared frame dependencies or conjunction outputs; and
949	- invalidation, stop and reconfiguration conditions.
950	
951	The actor may own its internal reasoning and search where the governing
952	method permits. It returns through the declared result relation. Hidden
953	internal reasoning is no substitute for required evidence, provenance or
954	authority (P6). Frame size is optimised for reliable evaluation, not for
955	maximum context loading: a more capable actor may activate a broader frame
956	and a less capable one may use a lawful refinement sequence, and both
957	preserve the same material invariants and authority relations (P0, P2;
958	RF-014).

961

963	frame for one evaluation. It may be written in Markdown, structured data, a
964	prompt or another consumer-selected carrier without changing the relation
965	(P0, RF-016).
966	
967	```markdown

969	
970	## Frame
971	- declaration identity and revision:
972	- exact evaluation and closed result algebra:
973

980	- exact source and semantic references:
981	- explicit exclusions and prohibited assumptions:
982	
983	## Actor And Authority

985	- semantic and evaluation authority:
986	- operation authority, subject, and territory where material:
987	- decision, acceptance, and publication authority:
988

620	
621	Roles are relations over steps that a configuration allocates
622	(Configuration above), not kinds of actor and not a fixed inventory.
623	Where a configuration's operations include construction, assessment or
624	disposition, this member names the responsibility for each: a
625	constructor owns the bounded implementation and its self-review; an
626	assessor evaluates a frozen candidate independently; a decision owner
627	disposes. A configuration may allocate other responsibilities. Where
628	independent assessment supports promotion, the assessor evaluates the
629	exact live subject, its authority paths, proof and installed state, not
630	the constructor's summary (EVALUATION §3). This preserves the
631	independent-review relation and prescribes no actor count: one actor may
632	occupy different roles across different claims when independence for the
633	assessed claim is preserved; no role name confers an operation
634	([RF-016](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-016-implementation-neutrality);
635	P6).
636	
637	The governing authority relation declares whether a bounded proxy may
638	accept and advance routine actions. Inside a step, a proxy so declared may
639	accept preservation, require local repair, reject a violating candidate
640	and advance to the next already-authorised action; what it cannot change,
641	and the re-entry such a change requires, is the proxy limit of
642	[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), which
643	this paragraph applies and does not restate. Human ceremony is not
644	required at every transition when the governing basis, the affected cone,

646	this delegation does not weaken direct human acceptance where the

649	When one capable context has sufficient existing work authority, exact

652	The applicable configuration (Configuration above) selects

654	independence need it; a role or frame name alone does not create that

657	carrier, the required assessment and the reserved decisions; it permits

662	independent assessment and reserves no acceptance, the constructor that

695	Qualified-reference guidance. Under

697	[AC-011](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-011-projection), a reference can supply
698	sufficient context when its accessible target and qualifications preserve
699	the consuming contract. Check the required subject and basis, assessment
700	standing, provenance, active obligation and version, and invalidators, rather
701	than candidate identity alone. A typed annotation supplies no evidence of
702	sufficiency by itself. Preserve the required body or a qualified resolvable
703	reference; no mandatory carrier or registry follows (P1, P3, P6).
704	
705	An exact local reference to a complete assessed record can preserve the
706	consumer-required distinctions. A candidate-only pointer can lose them when
707	unchanged candidate bytes have satisfied and indeterminate assessments that
708	require different continuations. A sufficiency claim relying on hash matching
709	states its collision and access assumptions. Unknown semantic relations retain their owning gap or
710	result; they do not all become one error class. A declared but unperformed
711	evaluation has no assessment result; an undeclared required capability is
712	a different condition. The [qualified-reference example](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md#qualified-references)
713	applies the sufficiency law owned by
714	[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation).

716	Given a seed set Z (the subject, outcome and affected relations named in the
717	intake), a relation family R (the dependency relations whose change can
718	alter the result, basis validity, evidence sufficiency or authority), and
719	the actor's envelope B:
720	
721	1. Compute the material closure of Z under R (AC-010,
722	   [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-010-material-closure)).

724	   exact, or the closure is not finite and unique on the exact basis,
725	   activation returns `closure_unresolved` (§3, Admission and activation)
726	   and no step proceeds; it does not guess.
727	2. Project the closure to the selected context, recording its boundary: the
728	   excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive
729	   seams (AC-011,
730	   [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-011-projection)).
731	   If the projection returns a gap or refusal, activation returns
732	   `closure_unresolved` and no step proceeds.
733	   Material not in the closure stays out; adjacent material does not enter
734	   because it exists
735	   ([RF-004](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-004-irrelevance-exclusion)).
736	3. Test fit against B. This step owns the size measurement and the fit
737	   test for the context dimension. Where B declares a context capacity,
738	   the size of the selected context is measured before the actor reads it,
739	   in the unit the capacity is declared in (bytes or tokens) and over the
740	   boundary that the selected execution binding states for it (§6), and is
741	   compared with that capacity. The measurement, the capacity and the
742	   outcome of the comparison are recorded before the read. A fit holds
743	   only for the measured boundary: context outside it is recorded as not
744	   measured, and no fit claim covers it. The fit claim for a measured

747	   supported upper bound that includes any host-supplied context; where

752	   context capacity, whatever question the step governs, because without
753	   it a fit claim against that capacity is an assertion, and a context
754	   that exceeds it would be cut without record
755	   ([RF-014](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-014-capability-fit)). It applies only
756	   there, because a resource control applies only through a selected frame
757	   and its owning scope
758	   ([REFERENCE_FRAME §4](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#frame-set-selection)), and a

760	   capacity, is no budget, and is not a universal measurement gate (P0,

763	   [RF-002](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-002-finite-attention) still apply. The size

938	## 3. Step results and disposition
939	
940	A step returns its results in the core algebra of
941	[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): each evaluation it
942	performed returns one core value with its predicate and domain outcome,
943	and an evaluation it did not perform has no result. The outcomes of
944	admitting and activating a step, and the step's own outcomes, answer other
945	questions than its evaluations do. This section owns them as five
946	refinements of the core. Each names the question it answers and the
947	predicate its mapping is for, and maps each of its values to exactly one
948	core value; the predicate travels with the value, so no refinement's
949	`satisfied` counts toward another predicate
950	([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)).
951	Purpose and material relation: admission, work, decisions and effects
952	stand in the one core (P5, P6), so a consumer that combines them cannot
953	read a refused activation as a step's stop, availability as fitness or
954	acceptance, a carried ambiguity as resolved, or an unknown effect as none.
955	
956	| Refinement | Question | Predicate of the mapping |
957	|---|---|---|
958	| admission and activation | may the step begin | the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact subject and basis |
959	| construction availability | did the step yield its output | a candidate is available |
960	| disposition | what the decision owner does with an assessed candidate | the candidate is accepted at its declared boundary |
961	| ambiguity outcome | what happened to a declared ambiguity | the declared ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis |
962	| effects | did an intended external effect occur | the intended effect occurred |
963	
964	A profile that refines these values for its own units maps each of its
965	values to exactly one core value under FOUNDATIONS §4 Results and adds no
966	core value.

974	subject and basis", and its cause selects its value (P5, P6; RF-005 for

976	refinement of [REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions),
977	which owns their causes, their predicate and their core values. Because
978	this predicate requires activation, a refused activation decides it with

1049	### Disposition
1050	
1051	The decision owner disposes an assessed candidate with one of four
1052	semantic dispositions (§1, Roles and delegation; P6, P5). An assessor may recommend one; the
1053	recommendation is evidence for the decision owner, never a disposition
1054	([EVALUATION §4](EVALUATION.md#4-review-results)). The disposition is the
1055	acceptance result: it consumes the candidate's availability and assessment
1056	results and stays separate from both (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results). Each maps
1057	to the core for the predicate "the candidate is accepted at its declared
1058	boundary":
1059	
1060	| Disposition | Condition | Core value |
1061	|---|---|---|
1062	| `accept` | the candidate closes its declared cone and preserves every affected governing relation | satisfied |
1063	| `local_repair` | implementation or proof is locally defective while the governing relation remains coherent | falsified |
1064	| `re_enter` | the governing outcome, a requirement, an identity, a lifecycle, an authority, a public contract or the accepted design must change | invalid_basis |
1065	| `reject` | the candidate violates a governing relation or leaves an undisposed competing truth path | falsified |
1066	
1067	For `local_repair` the local defect, and for `reject` the violated relation
1068	or the competing truth path, is the counterexample to accepting this
1069	candidate; a repaired candidate is a new candidate with its own results.
1070	For `re_enter` the governing basis the candidate was built and assessed on
1071	must change, so that basis cannot support acceptance; the change re-enters
1072	at its owning relation (§4). The core values place
1073	acceptance in the one core, as FOUNDATIONS §4 Results requires, so that a
1074	consumer combining results cannot take availability or assessment as
1075	acceptance (P6).

1077	Global correctness means conserving every global relation affected by the
1078	bounded action; it does not require proving the whole product inside every

1080	requires reassessment of the frame altitude, the causal cone, the common
1081	components, the design-versus-code placement and the authority
1082	sufficiency. The method sets no rejection-count threshold, mandatory
1083	review-round count or review state machine; it prohibits repeating an
1084	unchanged failed construction relation as if iteration alone could close

1087	### Ambiguity outcome
1088	
1089	A declared ambiguity is resolved, carried, escalated or blocked, and the
1090	outcome is recorded either way (§4, which also names the hard stops;
1091	[SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle)
1092	applies this to the method's chain of authority surfaces). Each outcome
1093	maps to the core for the predicate "the declared ambiguity is resolved on
1094	the exact basis" (P5, P6):
1095	
1096	| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
1097	|---|---|---|
1098	| `resolved` | satisfied | a decision was taken under the policy that permits lawful probabilistic processing, or by human adjudication, and recorded |
1099	| `carried` | falsified | policy permits work to continue with the ambiguity open; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and it stays a recorded residual that names the evidence or decision that would resolve it |
1100	| `escalated` | out_of_frame | policy or risk appetite reserves the decision to human adjudication, an authority the step does not hold; the value names that authority |
1101	| `blocked` | falsified | the ambiguity stays unresolved, and policy or a hard stop (§4) halts work at it; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and the value names the halting condition and what would lift it |
1102	
1103	An open ambiguity is a known state of the exact basis, so `carried` and
1104	`blocked` decide the predicate false; neither is `indeterminate`, whose
1105	evidence cannot decide the predicate. Each keeps its domain outcome with
1106	the value: `carried` with what would resolve the ambiguity, `blocked` with
1107	the halting condition and what would lift it (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results,
1108	Recording). No outcome other than `resolved` maps to `satisfied`, so a
1109	dependent claim cannot rest on a carried, escalated or blocked ambiguity
1110	as if it were resolved. The mapping places ambiguity outcomes
1111	in the one core, which FOUNDATIONS §4 Results requires of every outcome
1112	(P5, P6).

1114	### Effects
1115	
1116	An effectful step's intended external effect has one of three values,
1117	mapped for the predicate "the intended effect occurred", that is, the
1118	declared outcome of the effect is attained. The value turns on what the
1119	admitted evidence establishes about that outcome (P5 with the open-world
1120	premise, P6):
1121	
1122	| Value | Core value | Ground |
1123	|---|---|---|
1124	| `completed` | satisfied | evidence about the subject establishes that the intended effect occurred in full and that the effect has ended |
1125	| `not_effected` | falsified | evidence about the subject establishes that the declared outcome is not attained and that no later completion of the effect can attain it, for example where no effect began, the effect ended short, an interval that the declared outcome bounds has closed with part of it not done, or the part already done has itself made the declared outcome unattainable, as when it destroyed what the outcome needed; any part that did occur is named with the value |
1126	| `completion_unknown` | indeterminate | neither of the other values is established: the evidence cannot decide whether the intended effect has occurred or will occur, as for a request whose response was lost with no counterexample observed; or the evidence shows the intended effect in full while the effect may still be acting, and the outcome stays undecided until what the effect leaves on the subject is settled; its residual names the observation that would decide |
1127	
1128	`not_effected` requires evidence about the subject. A lost response, an
1129	absent record, or an actor's context that holds no trace of the effect is
1130	not that evidence, and the value stays `completion_unknown`.
1131	`completion_unknown` never maps to `completed` or to `not_effected`.
1132	
1133	Whether the effect has ended is a second question beside the predicate
1134	above, and it enters the value only as a conjunct of `completed`. An
1135	effect has ended where evidence about the subject establishes
1136	that it no longer acts on the subject or that it never began. Where an
1137	effect began and the evidence does not establish its end, the end is not
1138	established, and that is recorded beside the value as a residual naming
1139	the observation that would establish it. The end never decides a
1140	`not_effected` value and is never folded into one: when an interval that
1141	the declared outcome bounds has closed with part not done, the value is
1142	`not_effected` while the effect may still be acting. The residual does
1143	not weaken the counterexample, and the counterexample does not resolve
1144	the residual. `completed` alone requires the end established, so a
1145	counterexample stands without proof that the effect has ended, while
1146	success is never claimed for an effect that may still be acting
1147	([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Standing).
1148	
1149	An effect of uncertain completion is one whose value is
1150	`completion_unknown`, or whose value is `not_effected` with its end not
1151	established. §5 reconciles it, sufficiently for the next dependent
1152	action, before any repetition or dependent action. A `not_effected`
1153	value licenses neither treating the effect as absent nor repeating it
1154	while its end is not established.
1155	
1156	The refinement's material relation is whether an action whose
1157	external effect may have occurred is repeated or relied on; §4 names a
1158	lost post-effect response as a case that no added core value solves, and
1159	this refinement records it in the existing core. Keeping the end of the
1160	effect beside the value keeps two facts that one value would merge: a
1161	counterexample already established for the declared outcome, and an
1162	effect that may still be acting.

1370	## 5. Work state and restart
1371	
1372	Work state is the tuple of: the current persistent workspace; the governing
1373	basis; the applicable closed results and judgments with their invalidators;
1374	the residuals; and the known uncertainty over external effects. It is an
1375	object (P3); its carrier (files, an event stream, another admitted owner) is
1376	a profile or realisation choice. Resumption, checkpointing and the
1377	progress account of this section are generic procedures
1378	([SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding)): they require
1379	no particular carrier (P1, P6).
1380	
1381	Resumption is re-entry of the same method over the current work state,
1382	starting from the current material state, by a possibly different actor.
1383	It recovers applicable progress, re-checks the invalidators of each reused
1384	result (§7), reopens only affected support, and reconciles uncertain
1385	external effects, sufficiently for the next dependent action, before any
1386	repetition or dependent action. Resumption does not imply idempotence: an
1387	action whose external effect may have occurred is not repeated blindly;
1388	the lawful next moves are reconciliation, yield or stop.
1389	
1390	Checkpoint. Acceptance binds one exact checkpoint. The next
1391	already-authorised bounded action may begin without renewed human approval;
1392	acceptance does not widen the selected outcome or the affected relation set
1393	(P6, P2). A preservation checkpoint may retain unfinished or unaccepted
1394	work under an existing exact operation grant; it identifies its parent or
1395	predecessor, the included territory, the concurrent-writer disposition and
1396	the durable evidence location, and it is neither acceptance, promotion nor
1397	publication. A proposed restart, which reconstructs from less than the
1398	retained work, identifies why repair of retained work is insufficient,
1399	which obligations and evidence survive, and which causal assumptions
1400	change; reconstructability alone does not select reconstruction. The work state and reconciliation
1401	of uncertain effects preserve the retained progress and unresolved obligations
1402	(P0, P5 with the open-world premise).
1403	
1404	Progress is accepted material movement toward the selected outcome;
1405	prerequisite work names the obligation it enables; preservation and
1406	repeated proof are evidence, not new progress; rejected or superseded
1407	construction is churn; discovering previously hidden distance revises the
1408	forecast and is not negative progress. Paperwork, code volume, test count,
1409	commit count and review count are not progress by themselves. These are
1410	semantic categories, not a numeric progress algorithm; a consumer may
1411	derive its own progress and churn projections from them (P2). A member,
1412	profile or project that distinguishes finer categories for its own
1413	outcome states them as a refinement of these, naming this paragraph and
1414	mapping each of its categories to one of progress, prerequisite work,
1415	evidence that is not new progress, churn or forecast revision; a category
1416	it cannot map is a change to this owner, not a parallel category (P2, P6).

1458	### The workspace and an actor's account
1459	
1460	The workspace and its authoritative inputs persist across activations and
1461	are the continuing truth surface of the work: the surface whose current
1462	material state decides what the work has and has not done. An actor's
1463	context is an account of that state. It is bounded, because it is a
1464	projection of the state (§2); revisable, because an observation can
1465	correct it; and disposable, because a step records its closed results and
1466	step-produced facts before it returns (§1 Admission; P4b). An account is
1467	never a second truth surface, and no later activation needs a prior
1468	actor's context: its intake reconstructs the governing relations without

1708	applicability; a role, conversation or resumption change alone invalidates

576	## 11. The activation packet
577	
578	An actor receives one activated frame or one declared active frame
579	configuration, never an implied demand to reconstruct the complete
580	workspace from ambient context (P0). The minimum
581	activation packet contains:
582	
583	- frame identity and revision;
584	- the evaluation and its result algebra;
585	- the exact subject and basis;
586	- the material relations and applicable invariants;
587	- semantic, evaluation, operation where material, and decision authority;
588	- admissible evidence and tools;
589	- the capability and context envelope;
590	- exclusions and prohibited assumptions;
591	- declared frame dependencies or conjunction outputs; and
592	- invalidation, stop and reconfiguration conditions.
593	
594	The actor may own its internal reasoning and search where the governing
595	method permits. It returns through the declared result relation. Hidden
596	internal reasoning is no substitute for required evidence, provenance or
597	authority (P6). Frame size is optimised for reliable evaluation, not for
598	maximum context loading: a more capable actor may activate a broader frame
599	and a less capable one may use a lawful refinement sequence, and both
600	preserve the same material invariants and authority relations (P0, P2;
601	RF-014).

607	prompt or another consumer-selected carrier without changing the relation
608	(P0, RF-016).

610	```markdown

614	- declaration identity and revision:
615	- exact evaluation and closed result algebra:
616

620

623	- exact source and semantic references:
624	- explicit exclusions and prohibited assumptions:
625

628	- semantic and evaluation authority:
629	- operation authority, subject, and territory where material:
630	- decision, acceptance, and publication authority:
631

699	### Admission
700	
701	Drafting a step's contract and admitting it are distinct relations, even
702	inside one invocation that drafts, validates, admits and executes; no
703	separate turn, carrier or approval ceremony is implied by the distinction.
704	A contract carries at minimum the states drafted, admitted, rejected and
705	superseded ([TICKETS §5](../TICKETS.md#execution-contract-admission)).
706	Execution begins only after deterministic admission or an
707	explicit human override of the exact contract. The drafting actor never
708	infers admission from its own draft, from the presence of a carrier
709	(ticket, sprint entry, work contract), from lane placement or from an
710	`active` label. The admitted result identifies the admission mechanism and
711	its authority, the exact contract identity or digest, the decision and the
712	evidence, including any human override; absent those coordinates the
713	contract stays drafted or rejected, and prose asserting admission is not
714	admission evidence (P6; the actor cannot self-certify its own execution
715	basis). Admission validates the contract against its cited outcome,
716	prerequisite or experiment basis; it does not admit that basis, and
717	drafting, admitting or retaining a contract creates or renews no authority
718	its owner has not admitted (P6, P2;
719	[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](../FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What
720	creates no authority). Only an admitted contract activates a step: no
721	result, child completion, tool output, model response, shared actor or
722	lateral handoff activates another step or authorises continuation by
723	itself, and a profile that routes results names its instances of this
724	rule. Purpose and material relation: these admission conditions govern every
725	configuration, and their generic owner is this section (P6).
726	The admitted contract names one
727	durable result and evidence surface; every result, withheld closure and
728	residual obligation is recorded there before return, a conversation return
729	alone is not durable evidence, and if no such surface is authorised and
730	available, admission refuses (P4b). Absent or rejected admission returns
731	the missing work authority without execution, as `admission_refused` with
732	its cause ([§3 Admission and activation](../ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation)).
733	The selection of the carrier (ticket, sprint entry, run-scoped contract)
734	is owned by [TICKETS §5](../TICKETS.md#5-from-carrier-to-execution).

987	### Results
988	
989	Every performed evaluation returns one value of the core result algebra,
990	directly or as a refined value mapped into it (P5):
991	
992	| Value | Meaning |
993	|---|---|
994	| `satisfied` | the declared predicate holds on the exact basis |
995	| `falsified` | a declared counterexample defeats it |
996	| `indeterminate` | the available admissible evidence cannot decide it |
997	| `out_of_frame` | the evaluation requires an undeclared material relation or capability |
998	| `invalid_basis` | the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation |
999	
1000	This core is the only one. Results of constraints, judgments, frame
1001	evaluations, stops, work steps and effects are stated in it or in a
1002	refinement mapped into it, so that results from any members combine under
1003	one rule ([Conjunction of results](../FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)). Purpose and
1004	material relation: no combination can report success while a failure, an
1005	undecided question, an unperformed evaluation or an uncertain effect
1006	remains, and none of these can be mistaken for another (P5, P6).
1007	
1008	Recording. A result records its core value together with the predicate
1009	evaluated and the original domain outcome, which is the refined value
1010	where a refinement produced it. A mapping into the core never owns domain
1011	meaning: the member, profile or adopting Product that defines the refined
1012	value keeps it, and a consumer that needs the domain distinction reads the
1013	domain outcome, never the core value alone (P1, P6).
1014	
1015	Standing. The standing of a result is what it establishes about its
1016	predicate; it is distinct from the standing of a commitment (§1). Only
1017	`satisfied` establishes the predicate. `falsified` establishes that the
1018	predicate fails and names the counterexample. `indeterminate`,
1019	`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` establish neither, and each names what
1020	would decide: the evidence, the missing relation or capability with its
1021	owner where the subject gives one, or the basis repair. By support for the
1022	predicate, `satisfied` stands above each other value, and the other four
1023	are not ordered among themselves.
1024	
1025	No refinement or mapping raises a result's standing (P5, P6):
1026	
1027	- a falsified or failed result never maps to a satisfied or successful one;
1028	- a result that admissible evidence cannot decide never maps to
1029	  `satisfied`;
1030	- an evaluation that was not performed stays distinct from one whose
1031	  evidence cannot decide: it has no
1032	  [closed result](../ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), and it is never mapped
1033	  to `indeterminate` or to any other core value;
1034	- an effect whose completion is unknown never maps to no effect or to
1035	  completed.

1037	Not performed. An evaluation that is required or planned and was not
1038	performed has no closed result; an actor cannot report an evaluation it
1039	did not perform (P6). Nothing is coerced to success: a failed,
1040	indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope or invalid-basis result follows
1041	the declared result algebra and returns its own value under it, never
1042	`satisfied`, and a missing result, being no result, enters every
1043	conjunction over it as a gap: a planned assessment without a closed result

1046	RF-012 as a law over frames and

1053	answers and the predicate its mapping is for, and maps every refined value
